subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored `/exec` session overrides remain authoritative across restarts and config changes, or should operator `tools.exec.*` config regain authority when config changes?
rationale: The current behavior is documented and tested as persistent session state, but the report shows a plausible security-administration gap when a global exec policy is tightened after a session override exists.

options.title: Preserve compatibility plus add reset
options.body: Keep persistent `/exec` defaults as the default contract, but add a clear operator reset/doctor/session-patch path and docs for clearing stale exec overrides after policy changes.

options.title: Make config authoritative
options.body: Change precedence so changed global or agent `tools.exec.*` policy overrides stored session exec fields, accepting an upgrade behavior change for users relying on persistent session defaults.

options.title: Stop persisting `/exec`
options.body: Treat `/exec` as ephemeral turn/session runtime state only, which is simpler for security posture but breaks the current documented persistence model most aggressively.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility plus add reset
recommendation.body: Keep persistent `/exec` defaults as the default contract, but add a clear operator reset/doctor/session-patch path and docs for clearing stale exec overrides after policy changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about exec security policy and upgrade behavior, and recent merged exec-policy work makes this the closest routing signal among the history candidates.
